claims.author: hodlinator
claims.quote: For singleton types (`*Man` etc), in cases where it really leads to less logical groupings of fields, one could opt out, like we do for recursion warnings today.
claims.request: Allow opting out for singleton types (*Man etc.) when reorganizing fields leads to less logical grouping.

claims.author: bartoli
claims.question: Why does CI output warn about a loss of 11 padding bytes if the configured limit is supposed to be higher?
claims.quote: It seems the limit of 23 is not properly used though, since the CI output warns about a loss of 11 padding bytes?

claims.author: jonatack
claims.quote: consider keeping guarded members near their mutex and avoiding churn or grouping members less logically where it provides negligible benefit (arguably the changes in rpc/client.cpp and txmempool.h)
claims.request: Keep guarded members near their mutex and avoid churn or grouping members less logically where the benefit is negligible (such as in rpc/client.cpp and txmempool.h).

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: Reordering fields to eliminate padding makes code harder to read by splitting apart fields that belong together.
claims.quote: This could make the code harder to read by having fields that belong together split further apart.

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: So my preference would be to have this opt-in per-struct and accommodate each change with a measurement, or at least a guess of how much it would save.
claims.request: Make the check opt-in per-struct for types instantiated thousands of times and accompanied by measurements of savings.

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: if memory usage was a concern here, those should be string_view
claims.request: Use std::string_view in rpc/client.cpp if memory usage is a concern.

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: Splitting up rolling mempool fields harms readability for no benefit.
claims.quote: splitting this up makes the code harder to read for no benefit?
